newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Net premiums flat in 1996 for Bermuda insurers.
newsitem.headline: Net premiums flat in 1996 for Bermuda insurers.

text.p: Net premiums written were flat at $3.0 billion in 1996 for a group of Bermuda's biggest insurers, according to figures released by the Bermuda Registrar of Companies.
That compares with growth in net premiums written of 15 percent in 1995, the figures showed.

Bermuda's Class 4 insurers, such as ACE Ltd, EXEL Ltd and PartnerRe Ltd, are excess liability and property catastrophe firms underwriting non-related, open market risks. They are required to maintain minimum capital and surplus of $100 million.
Although net premiums written were flat, gross premiums written rose 10 percent to $3.4 billion in 1996.
But that still was down from 1995, when gross premiums written rose 19 percent.
Capital and surplus growth also slowed in 1996, the figures showed.
Capital and surplus rose 13 percent to $8.9 billion in 1996 for the Class 4 insurers, down from a 23 percent increase in 1995.
Total assets rose 12 percent to 16.5 billion in 1996. In 1995, total assets rose 32 percent.
Bermuda Registrar Kymn Astwood said the new statistics demonstrate the Bermuda insurance industry's ability to produce strong results despite weak market conditions.
Astwood said the changes in the gross and net premium writings reflect an increasingly "ultra conservative" approach to underwriting.

"It seems to us that the conservative nature of the underwriting strategies of these companies clearly demonstrates a commitment to security and claims paying ability and a laudable policy of resisting the temptation to write business at the wrong price," he said.
